why: A first-party documented route-builder flow that moves from freeform point placement to explicit reversible edits, a measurable review, and a location-aware choice to navigate or save. It is a compact reference for keeping an exploratory mobile task recoverable without asking users to commit too early.
taskGoal: Create, review, and optionally save a walking or hiking route before starting directions.

screens.purpose: Choose an accessible place on the map and enter route creation through the place's secondary actions.
screens.evidence: Apple documents opening a place, choosing More, then creating a custom route.

screens.purpose: Place route points and revise the path with local undo, reverse, out-and-back, close-loop, and point-removal controls.
screens.evidence: The official guide names point placement plus reversible route and point editing operations.

screens.purpose: Review distance, elevation profile, and estimated time before selecting a next action.
screens.evidence: Apple describes these route-summary values after the route is complete.

screens.purpose: Offer Directions near the route's start, Go when farther away, or Save Route to preserve the work.
screens.evidence: The documented completion choices depend on the user's proximity to the start and include optional saving.

screens.purpose: Name the route, optionally add notes, and complete the saved-route action.
screens.evidence: Apple's save flow requests a name and permits notes before completion.

transitions.contract: Do not enter drawing mode until the user has selected a place and deliberately chosen route creation.
Keep route edits reversible while placing points; show route metrics only after a coherent path exists.
Choose the primary navigation action from the user's proximity to the route start instead of forcing the same next step everywhere.
Saving is optional and late in the flow, so exploratory construction is not blocked by naming or note entry.

platformConstraints: Custom routes and their capabilities are not available in every country or region.
Downloading a route requires the Download Routes setting to be enabled; hiking-route search requires an internet connection.
The navigation handoff changes with physical proximity to the route's starting point.

exceptionStates.recovery: Expose the download prerequisite before a user depends on an offline route, rather than discovering it only during navigation.

exceptionStates.scenario: Feature is unavailable in the current region
exceptionStates.recovery: State the availability limit plainly and avoid presenting unsupported route-building controls as actionable.

exceptionStates.scenario: User wants to abandon or correct part of a route
exceptionStates.recovery: Keep undo, point removal, reverse, and loop conversions inside the builder so correction does not reset the whole task.

capture.attribution: Apple Inc.; Apple Maps documentation in the iPhone User Guide.
capture.reusePolicy: inspiration-only — record the documented task structure and constraints; do not reuse Apple Maps screens, cartography, icons, imagery, names, or marks. The local preview is an original abstract diagram.
